invariants: the request tenant comes only from the authenticated identity and is repeated in every index, object and manifest lookup
job, frozen request, history, audit and outbox acceptance facts commit atomically
the worker is deployed compatible and idle before the writer or dispatcher can be enabled
PCAP source selection uses the M02 versioned pcap index and immutable object receipt
session and file restoration calls the M03 versioned restoration interface and never creates a second reassembly algorithm
restored content is treated as inert bytes and is never executed, imported or rendered as active content on the server
temporary objects become published only after size, hash, manifest and object-version verification
accepted is not completed; partial, corrupt, oversize, missing object, bad hash, expired source and cross-tenant states are explicit
retry resumes from an immutable checkpoint and cannot publish a duplicate object or manifest
download requires a short-lived purpose-bound authorization and a durable audit before bytes are returned
retention cleanup refuses a referenced object, legal hold, active lease, unmatched manifest or unexpired download grant
domain.compensation: stop new intake, disable writer and worker flags, let each accepted job complete, fail or cancel under its frozen policy, restore the legacy API/UI route, retain objects and manifests, and reconcile orphan objects, leases, outbox, inbox and final states

data.migration: additive forensics job/history/outbox/checkpoint/manifest/download-audit schema under T1-M09-N009/N010; no destructive cleanup

negative_tests: cross-tenant job, source index, object key, manifest, checkpoint and audit access is rejected
a caller with pcap:read cannot create, cancel, retry, cut, presign or download
a caller with pcap:write but without pcap:download cannot receive bytes or a signed URL
expired or wrong-purpose signed authorization is rejected and audited
an alert or case reference from another tenant creates no accepted job

journeys: small synchronous cut below the approved time and size threshold
asynchronous multi-object cut and session restoration
file restoration with partial and corrupt streams
stop_conditions: a bounded limit is exceeded without async fallback, memory or disk budget is exceeded, duplicate objects appear, checkpoint recovery diverges, or status P99 exceeds the approved candidate

tests: G0 canonical owner, state, permission, manifest, compatibility and rollback contract
G1 PostgreSQL acceptance atomicity, idempotency, revision, cancel and retry races
G2 compatible-idle worker readiness followed by default-off writer and dispatcher enablement
G3 M02 pcap index to MinIO source receipt to M03 session and file restoration to derived manifest
G4 interruption, partial, corrupt, oversize, object missing, wrong hash, expiry and cross-tenant negatives
G5 PG, Kafka, ClickHouse and MinIO final-state count, hash and watermark reconciliation
G6 K8s rollback, observation, orphan and retention reconciliation
G7 Windows Chrome refresh recovery, controlled download, verification and evidence export
evidence: same-candidate request, job, history, audit, outbox, Kafka offset, source index, source object receipt, restoration manifest, derived object hash, chain-of-custody, final state, download audit, rollback and browser journey
